1.

Heard Ms. Pooja Singh Advocate, holding brief of Shri Desh Raj Singh Yadav, learned counsel for
the appellant-applicant, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.

2. This bail application has been moved on behalf of applicant, who was convicted by the judgment
and order dated 21.01.2025 passed by Additional District and Sessions Judge, Court No.3,
Ayodhya/Faizabad in Sessions Trial No.213/2018 arising out of Case Crime No.98/2018, under
Sections 498A, 306 I.P.C., Police Station- Khandasa District- Ayodhya/Faizabad.

entities.text:
Additional District and Sessions Judge, Court No.3,
Ayodhya/Faizabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 3.  Learned counsel for the appellant submits that appellant is a lady and she has been falsely implicated in the present case.
He further submits that the trial court while convicting the appellant has failed to appreciate the fact that sufficient evidences to attract Section 306 IPC are missing.

He further submits that the victim died on her own which is evident from the perusal of the Parcha No.6 of case diary and the statement of Investigating Officer that the deceased set herself on fire with the intention to commit suicide.
It is also undisputed fact that in-laws of the deceased took her to the hospital and father-in-law of the deceased informed parents of the deceased about the alleged incident.
He further submits that the appellant is mother-in-law of the deceased and there are sweeping allegations against her in the prosecution case but no specific role has been assigned to her.
He further submits that during the course of trial, the appellant was on bail and she never misused the liberty of bail granted to her.
4. Theapplicant is in jail since 21.01.2025.
It is further submitted that there is no likelihood that this appeal may be heard in near future whereas the speedy justice is the fundamental rights of theapplicant.
Theapplicant has every hope of success in the appeal.
5. Learned A.G.A. opposes the prayer for bail and submits that conviction of the appellant is on the basis of evidence on record.

6. In the above-mentioned facts and circumstances of the case and the fact that the appellant is in jail since 21.01.2025 and she has no previous criminal history, I find it a fit case for enlarging the applicant on bail.
Accordingly, bail application is allowed.

7. Letapplicant Saroj be released on bail in the aforesaid sessions trial on her furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The copy of bail bonds be furnished to this Court after accepting it by the C.J.M./court concerned.
